name: CJC-1295 with DAC

card.summary: A long-acting GHRH analogue (drug affinity complex) talked about for growth hormone stacks; unapproved and with no appearance trials behind it.
card.note: Unapproved peptide; community talk rests on anecdote.

quick.overview:
CJC-1295 with DAC is a long-acting version of a GHRH analogue, meant to make the pituitary release more growth hormone. Forum users pair it with ipamorelin or tesamorelin for muscle and body-composition goals.

The community material is thin and anecdotal, and there are no cited trials of it for appearance.
quick.mechanism: It mimics GHRH at the pituitary, and the DAC attachment binds blood proteins to prolong its action versus the version without DAC.
quick.risks: It is not an approved medicine and risks in healthy users have not been defined by the sources used here. Forum discussions focus on combinations rather than safety data.

lead: CJC-1295 with DAC (also called DAC:GRF) is a synthetic analogue of growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH) developed by ConjuChem Biotechnologies. A drug affinity complex (DAC) added to the peptide binds albumin in the blood, which extends how long it stays active compared with shorter-acting GHRH analogues such as the version without DAC (modified GRF 1-29).[1]

People in bodybuilding and looksmaxxing communities discuss it as a way to raise growth hormone (GH) and IGF-1 levels in pursuit of leaner, more muscular physiques, better sleep and recovery, and, among younger users, height and facial bone changes.[2][3][4] It is often described alongside ipamorelin or GHRPs such as GHRP-6, and sometimes tesamorelin.[2][5][6]

Wikipedia reports that in human subjects a single injection raised plasma GH two- to ten-fold for six days or longer and IGF-1 for roughly nine to eleven days, with an estimated half-life of about six to eight days.[1] It has not been approved as a medicine. Its development for lipodystrophy and GH deficiency reached phase II trials before being stopped after a participant died; the attending physician attributed the death to likely unrelated coronary disease, but the programme was ended as a precaution.[1]

chain: Peptide stimulates the pituitary to release more growth hormone
GH and IGF-1 levels rise for days
Users report leaner body composition, recovery and sleep gains; some hope for height or facial growth
angle.text: Users take GHRH analogues to push GH and IGF-1 higher, with the aim of building muscle, losing fat and recovering faster, which together change physique. Younger users on forums also ask about height and facial bone growth, which are community hopes rather than documented outcomes.

infobox: CJC-1295 without DAC (modified GRF 1-29), tesamorelin, ipamorelin

paras: CJC-1295 is a modified form of GHRH (1-29) carrying a maleimidopropionyl lysine at the C-terminus that forms the drug affinity complex and binds albumin.[1] Wikipedia notes that CJC-1295 and modified GRF (1-29), also called CJC-1295 without DAC, are sometimes wrongly treated as the same compound in papers; the latter lacks the DAC group and has a much shorter duration of action.[1]

The peptide acts at the GHRH receptor on the pituitary to stimulate GH release, which in turn raises IGF-1. The DAC extension prolongs its presence in the bloodstream, so IGF-1 levels stay elevated for days to weeks after dosing.[1] Wikipedia reports elevated IGF-1 for up to 28 days after multiple doses.[1]

ConjuChem developed the compound for lipodystrophy and growth hormone deficiency, and it reached phase II clinical trials. The trial was discontinued after the death of a participant; the investigator's view was that the likely cause was asymptomatic coronary artery disease with plaque rupture and not the drug, but research was ended as a precaution.[1] It is not approved for medical use, and it is sold in the research-peptide market that forum users describe.

On looksmax.org, CJC-1295 with DAC appears in questions about peptide stacks, such as combining it with ipamorelin or tesamorelin. In one thread a user asked whether adding tesamorelin was dangerous; a reply argued there was no point in stacking several GHRH analogues and GHRPs and favoured the no-DAC version with ipamorelin.[2]

Teenage users ask about the combination for height, sleep and facial bone growth, and ask whether growth plates would be affected; replies mostly redirect to HGH or dispute the height benefit.[3][4] Another user asked about pairing it with teriparatide.[7] On T Nation, older threads discuss it with GHRP-6 or modified GRF, and one 67-year-old poster described nightly ipamorelin and CJC-1295 with DAC as raising his IGF-1 from a very low level over three months.[5][6][8] These are anecdotes, and the wiki does not give dosing or sourcing instructions.

No studies found testing CJC-1295 with DAC for muscle, body composition or appearance. Early human pharmacology studies of the compound, cited by Wikipedia, measured GH and IGF-1 responses in healthy adults.[1] The phase II trial in lipodystrophy and GH deficiency was ended after one participant's death.[1]

timeline.event: ConjuChem develops DAC:GRF and runs early human pharmacology studies of GH and IGF-1 response.[1]
Phase II trial for lipodystrophy and GH deficiency stopped after a participant died.[1]
T Nation members discuss combining CJC-1295 forms with GHRP-6.[5][9]
looksmax.org threads ask about stacking it with ipamorelin and tesamorelin.[2]

lore.intro: CJC-1295 with DAC is discussed on looksmax.org and T Nation as a GH-boosting peptide, usually in stacks with ipamorelin or GHRPs.[2][5][8]

claims.claim: Using several GHRH analogues together gives a bigger result.
claims.believers: One looksmax.org poster reasoned that more GHRH analogues, such as tesamorelin plus CJC-1295 DAC, should give a greater effect.[2]
claims.experts: No published studies have tested multiple GHRH analogues together for muscle or appearance outcomes.

claims.claim: The no-DAC version with ipamorelin is preferable to the DAC version.
claims.believers: A looksmax.org reply favoured the no-DAC version with ipamorelin; T Nation members described pulses of GH from pairing modified GRF with GHRP-6.[2][5][9]
claims.experts: Wikipedia notes the DAC version keeps GH and IGF-1 raised for days, while the shorter version lacks the extension; no head-to-head appearance study exists.[1]

claims.claim: It can add height or facial bone growth in teenagers.
claims.believers: Teen posters ask about it for height and facial bone growth with open growth plates; one reply suggested HGH instead.[3][4]
claims.experts: No published studies have tested CJC-1295 for height or facial bone growth.

claims.claim: It restores low IGF-1 and improves recovery in older users.
claims.believers: A 67-year-old T Nation poster reported much higher IGF-1 after three months of nightly ipamorelin and CJC-1295 with DAC.[8]
claims.experts: Wikipedia reports that it raises GH and IGF-1 in humans; effects on physique have not been tested in published trials.[1]
